learning_outcomes.text: Have knowledge and understanding of thermodynamics and heat transfer.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of thermal engineering.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve thermodynamics and heat transfer problems using established methods.
Be able to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Have technical and laboratory skills.
Be able to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve thermodynamics and heat transfer problems.
Understand applicable methods and techniques in thermodynamics and heat transfer and their limitations.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory skills.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem solving within their area of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Review of previous thermodynamics concepts acquired by the student, thermodynamic properties, T-s diagram of water, incompressible liquid and ideal gas models.
Mass, energy and entropy balances in closed systems.
Mass, energy and entropy balances in open systems.
Steady-state devices: nozzles, diffusers, pumps, compressors, turbines, open and closed heat exchangers, and valves.
Introduction to heat transfer. Heat transfer mechanisms: Fourier's Law, Newton's Law of Cooling, Stefan-Boltzmann Law.
One-dimensional steady-state conduction with and without heat generation. Planar, cylindrical and spherical geometries. Thermal resistances.
Fins: formulation, design and analysis of performance and efficiency. Finned surfaces.
teaching_methods: Combined classes where knowledge students must acquire will be presented and problems related to the knowledge to be presented will be solved.
Resolution of exercises by the student to self-assess their knowledge and acquire the necessary skills.

Development of practical work. Preparation of reports presenting the results obtained in the laboratory and/or through computer software. The student's ability to present results clearly and concisely, as well as their discussion, will be valued.
assessment_rules: The default weighting is: Laboratory practices (15%), Partial exam (25%), Final exam (60%). If the partial exam score is 5 or higher, the weighting changes to: Laboratory practices (15%), Partial exam (50%), Final exam (35%). A minimum score of 4.5 is required in each part of the course.
